concepts.title: Nervous System - Neurons and Reflex Action
concepts.definition: The nervous system controls and coordinates through neurons that carry electrochemical signals: a reflex action like withdrawing a hand from a flame travels through the spinal cord's reflex arc without waiting for the brain, while the brain handles thinking, balance and memory.
concepts.key_idea: Reflex arc short-circuits danger: spinal cord acts first, brain learns later.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc106.txt sections on animals - nervous system, reflex actions, human brain

solution_steps.explain: Receptors sense heat, touch or pressure and fire signals.
Sensory neuron to spinal cord, relay neuron, then motor neuron.
The muscle contracts and pulls the hand away instantly.

concepts.title: Coordination in Plants
concepts.definition: Plants coordinate without nerves: they respond to touch (mimosa folding), light (phototropism bending shoots), gravity and water using chemical signals - plant hormones like auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin and abscisic acid direct growth in the needed direction.
concepts.key_idea: No nerves needed: plant hormones bend growth toward light and away from harm.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc106.txt sections on coordination in plants, hormones
question_patterns: how does the mimosa plant respond to touch - explain the immediate response

solution_steps.explain: Light, gravity, touch or water starts the response.
Auxin gathers away from light, making shaded cells elongate.
Differential growth bends the plant toward or away from the stimulus.

concepts.title: Hormones in Animals - Chemical Coordination
concepts.definition: Endocrine glands pour hormones into the blood to reach target organs: the thyroid controls metabolism, insulin from the pancreas lowers blood sugar, adrenaline prepares fight-or-flight, and the pituitary masters the other glands - completing chemical coordination alongside nerves.
concepts.key_idea: Glands whisper through blood: hormones reach only the organs that listen.

solution_steps.explain: Each endocrine gland secretes specific hormones into blood.
Hormones act only on cells carrying their receptors.
Too little or too much hormone causes named disorders.
